source_name: CBK — Regulation on Cash Operations / plan to facilitate implementation (news + legal framework)
why_relevant: The authoritative text of the measure at the centre of this cell: Regulation on Cash Operations adopted by the CBK Governing Board 27 Dec 2023, in force 1 Feb 2024, plus the transition/deadline plan (three-month facilitation period, mobile banking units, ATM deployment and dinar-euro exchange facilitation in the four northern municipalities). Deadlines and enforcement steps originate here.

source_name: BQK — KOS-GIRO standard document / QR code standardisation guideline
why_relevant: KOS-GIRO is the national bill-payment slip standard; CBK has separately approved a Guideline (Udhëzim) standardising the payment QR code aligned to the EPC QR standard. Together these are the domestic payment-standards layer feeding merchant/POS and bill-payment interoperability.

source_name: BQK — Lista e institucioneve financiare të licencuara/regjistruara (dated consolidated register PDF, ALB)
why_relevant: The actual machine-harvestable register artefact: name, address, contact of every licensed bank, MFI, NBFI, insurer, insurance intermediary, pension fund and money-transfer/exchange entity, versioned by date in the URL. This is the highest-value single file in the cell.

source_name: BQK-hosted consolidated law texts (sq/sr) — Ligji Nr. 08/L-304 për Bankat / Zakon br. 08/L-304 o bankama
why_relevant: New banking law (gazetted as Official Gazette No. 2, 27 January 2026 per the Serbian version's header) — the enabling act that will force a wave of BQK secondary regulation and transition deadlines during the tracking window. BQK hosts both language versions.

source_name: BQK — Regulation on the Authorization and Governance of Payment Institutions and E-Money Institutions and Registration of AISP (B15)
why_relevant: Core licensing rule for payment institutions, e-money institutions and account information service providers — the gating document for any new payments market entrant in Kosovo. Approved by the CBK Board in mid-2026, i.e. the current PSD2-aligned regime.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për qasjen e ofruesve të shërbimeve të pagesave jo-banka në sistemet e pagesave (non-bank PSP access to payment systems)
why_relevant: Sets the conditions under which non-bank PSPs/EMIs can access KIPS and interconnected systems — the key structural rule for fintech participation in clearing, and a SEPA-alignment requirement (settlement finality / access).

source_name: Ligji Nr. 04/L-155 për Sistemin e Pagesave (Law on the Payment System)
why_relevant: The enabling statute under which all CBK payment regulations are issued; every regulation cites it in its preamble. Needed as the baseline against which the new Law on Payment Services (2026) supersedes/amends provisions.

source_name: CBK / BQK — English-language legal texts (?lang=en PDF variants)
why_relevant: Confirmed English translations of Kosovo financial legislation published by the regulator itself — e.g. Law No. 04/L-093 on Banks, MFIs and NBFIs as printed in Official Gazette No. 11 of 11 May 2012, plus reporting manuals. Essential for the cell's 'English translations' leg, and the ?lang= query-string convention generalises across the CBK document library.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për IBAN / Sistemi i Numrave Standardë të Llogarive Bankare
why_relevant: Defines the Kosovo IBAN/BAN standard — a hard technical prerequisite for SEPA scheme participation and for any cross-border payment routing work. Version history shows the standard being reissued as SEPA alignment progresses.

source_name: BQK — Manuali i mbikëqyrjes së bazuar në rrezik për banka (risk-based supervision manual)
why_relevant: Discloses how BQK actually supervises: examination cycle, risk-rating methodology, escalation. Predicts what supervisors will demand of banks and vendors ahead of any formal rule change.

source_name: Banka Qendrore e Republikës së Kosovës — Rregullore për parandalimin e pastrimit të parave (AML regulation for licensed institutions)
why_relevant: The AML rulebook is split: the FIU issues udhëzime for all reporting entities, while the CBK issues the binding prudential regulation for licensed banks/MFIs/PSPs (including the newer regulation on information accompanying transfers of funds and crypto-asset transfers). Boundary source for this cell — needed to know which deadline comes from which publisher. Available in sq, sr and en.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për Instrumentet e Pagesave Elektronike
why_relevant: Rule governing issuance of electronic payment instruments (cards, e-wallets) and the requirement to be licensed by CBK before offering them — directly relevant to card scheme, POS and acquiring market entry conditions.

source_name: BQK — Manuali i Licencimit Bankar / Manuali i Regjistrimit të IMF dhe IFJB / Manuali i Licencimit të Siguruesve
why_relevant: Licensing manuals define the application procedure, documentary requirements and statutory decision deadlines for banks, MFIs/NBFIs and insurers — the procedural spine behind every register entry and a direct source of 'deadlines' content.

source_name: ZAKON BR. 08/L-304 O BANKAMA — Serbian-language gazetted text
why_relevant: Serbian is an official language of Kosovo and gazette texts are published in it; the Serbian version is the practical reading route for Serb-community institutions and for cross-checking translation of deadline clauses ('stupanje na snagu'). Also the anchor for Serbian-language query expansion in this cell.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për emetimin e parasë elektronike (E-money issuance regulation, sq/en)
why_relevant: States the CBK obligation to publish a register of licensed/registered electronic money issuers and sets the conditions and deadlines for that licence class — the legal hook for the e-money slice of the register.

source_name: BQK — Godišnji Izveštaj (CBK Annual Report, Serbian edition)
why_relevant: Serbian-language edition of the annual report — the main confirmed sr-language CBK artefact found. Establishes the sr terminology set (nadzor, licencirane banke, kaznene mere) needed for Serbian-language monitoring of Kosovo supervision.

source_name: BQK Strategic Roadmap on Climate & Environmental Risk Management (example of a BQK document explicitly released for public consultation)
why_relevant: Concrete evidence that BQK does run public consultation on supervisory documents and records the consultation history inside the document itself. Establishes the document-internal consultation trail as an extraction target when no separate consultation page exists.

source_name: IMF Financial Sector Stability Review for Kosovo (hosted on BQK site, sq/sr/en)
why_relevant: External assessment of the Kosovo supervisory regime with explicit recommendations; BQK regulatory agendas frequently follow FSSR recommendations, so it is a leading indicator of which rules will be drafted next.

source_name: FSDK depositor-information leaflet in Serbian (hosted on BQK education site)
why_relevant: Confirms FSDK material is published in Serbian and gives the sr terminology (osiguranje depozita, nivo pokrića) needed to search Serbian-language Kosovo sources.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: GZK — LIGJI NR. 05/L-096 për Parandalimin e Pastrimit të Parave dhe Luftimin e Financimit të Terrorizmit
why_relevant: The AML/CFT statute (voted in plenary 25 May 2016, gazetted June 2016) that drives customer due-diligence and reporting obligations for banks, payment institutions and the FIU. AML statutes in Kosovo are amended repeatedly under EU-alignment and MONEYVAL pressure, so this act page is a recurring deadline generator. Predecessor act 03/L-196 also on GZK, useful for lineage.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: GZK — LIGJI NR. 03/L-209 për Bankën Qendrore të Republikës së Kosovës (CBK statute record)
why_relevant: The enabling statute cited as legal basis in essentially every CBK regulation ('Bazuar në nenin 35/36 ... të Ligjit nr. 03/L-209'). Any amendment to it changes the CBK's rule-making authority and therefore the whole downstream regulation stack — a high-leverage statute to watch in the Assembly pipeline.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Ministria e Financave, Punës dhe Transfereve (MFPT) — National AML/CFT Strategy and action plan
why_relevant: The FIU sits under the Ministry of Finance; MFPT publishes the Strategjia Kombëtare against money laundering/terrorist financing with a dated action plan. Those action-plan milestones are the government-side deadlines that translate PECK/EU recommendations into national obligations, and MFPT also runs the appointment of the FIU Director.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Projektligji për Shërbimet e Pagesave (Draft Law on Payment Services) — Office of the Prime Minister
why_relevant: The PSD2-transposing draft law (Government Decision No. 08/08, 3 April 2026) introducing open banking, TPP access and the modern PI/EMI regime. Its entry into force is an explicit precondition for Kosovo's final SEPA application. An earlier 2024 version also exists, enabling version-diffing of the policy trajectory.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Draft law amending Law No. 05/L-096 on AML/CFT (Projektligji, Office of the Prime Minister)
why_relevant: A live 2026 amendment to the core AML/CFT law — the single highest-value forward-looking regulatory signal in this cell. Government-approved draft text published on the PM's office site indicates changes to obligations, thresholds and possibly filing deadlines before they hit the gazette.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Kosovo Ministry of European Integration / Government — PKZMSA (National Programme for Implementation of the SAA)
why_relevant: The national mirror of EU conditionality: PKZMSA lists, per acquis chapter and per year, the exact Kosovo laws and sub-legal acts to be drafted to transpose EU financial-services and AML instruments, with responsible institution and target quarter. This is the operational deadline register for banking/payments rulemaking.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Office of the Prime Minister — Programi për Reforma në Ekonomi (Economic Reform Programme, ERP)
why_relevant: The ERP is an annually updated commitment document negotiated with the European Commission; its financial-sector chapter pre-announces planned laws and regulations with target years. Not a legal act, so it never appears in regulation searches — a classic indirect artefact for this cell.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Rregullorja Nr. 05/2016 për Standardet Minimale të Procesit të Konsultimit Publik + Udhëzuesi për procesin e konsultimeve publike
why_relevant: The rulebook that defines what a Kosovo consultation legally is: minimum comment periods, mandatory publication on the platform, and the duty to publish a results report. Without it you cannot tell whether an observed short deadline is normal or a procedural shortcut worth flagging.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Office of the Prime Minister — Concept Document on Developing the Regulatory Framework for Financial Markets
why_relevant: Concept documents (koncept-dokument) are the mandated pre-legislative step in Kosovo; this one signals the direction of future financial-market legislation and therefore of BQK's future rulemaking and supervisory perimeter — a forward indicator ahead of any draft regulation.

entity_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës
source_name: Zyra e Kryeministrit — performance/oversight reports on independent agencies (e.g. ARKEP report)
why_relevant: Government/Assembly-level reviews of independent regulators expose governance gaps, board vacancies and rulemaking backlogs — a leading indicator of whether a regulator can actually deliver a pending rule on schedule.

source_name: World Bank Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project (P507881)
why_relevant: Live EUR ~50m operation financing establishment of a Development Bank, capitalisation of financial institutions, credit guarantee expansion and a fast payment system. Its results framework and legal covenants are effectively a dated roadmap for Kosovo payments-infrastructure regulation — highest-value single document for the payments workstream.

source_name: World Bank Kosovo Systematic Country Diagnostic (Update, Report 169605-XK) and earlier SCD 114618-XK
why_relevant: Sets the analytical frame the Bank uses to justify financial-sector conditions — access to finance, cash intensity, payment costs. Gives baseline diagnostics (e.g. retail payments cost study methodology) that later reappear as programme targets.

source_name: ATK fiscal-device functional and technical specifications (PDF series)
why_relevant: The actual conformance spec a device or POS integration must meet to be certified in Kosovo — requirements, functional and technical characteristics of electronic fiscal devices. Successive editions (Mars 2014, Qershor 2015, and any SEF-era replacement) are the engineering-level requirement baseline.

source_name: ATK tax legislation compendia (Libri i Ligjeve / Doracaku i TVSH-së)
why_relevant: Consolidated law-and-instruction books and VAT handbooks published by ATK; they bundle the tax-procedure law, VAT law and their implementing administrative instructions, including e-invoice obligations for internet supplies (UA Nr. 02/2018 on use of electronic devices and fiscal systems). Convenient authoritative baseline text.

source_name: ATK legislation library in Serbian (Legjislacioni tatimor i Kosovës në gjuhën serbe)
why_relevant: Confirms ATK publishes its tax legislation corpus in Serbian, giving a second-language entry point (poreska administracija, fiskalne kase, pravilnik) for monitoring and for serving Serb-majority municipalities. Useful for glossary building and for catching sr-only republications.

entity_name: EBRD news and project announcements for Kosovo banks
source_name: EBRD Kosovo Country Strategy 2022-2027
why_relevant: Board-approved statement of EBRD policy-dialogue priorities in Kosovo including financial-sector deepening, capital-market development and NPL/credit-infrastructure work; strategies are consulted publicly and signal where EBRD will push for legal/regulatory change.

entity_name: EBRD news and project announcements for Kosovo banks
source_name: EBRD Financial Sector Strategy 2026-2030 (and 2021-2025 predecessor)
why_relevant: Sector-wide doctrine that determines what EBRD will finance and what regulatory reforms it will make a precondition across the Western Balkans, Kosovo included. Published in draft for public comment, so it front-runs country-level conditionality.

entity_name: EBRD news and project announcements for Kosovo banks
source_name: EBRD — Kosovo Country Strategy (Albanian edition)
why_relevant: IFI country strategies state intended policy-dialogue and technical-cooperation priorities for the financial sector over a multi-year horizon — i.e. which regulatory reforms an IFI intends to push and fund. Published in Albanian, which also yields local regulatory vocabulary.

entity_name: EBRD news and project announcements for Kosovo banks
source_name: EBRD Kosovo Country Diagnostic: Private investment challenges and opportunities (2022)
why_relevant: Underpinning evidence base for the country strategy; contains the financial-sector constraints analysis (credit depth, capital markets, collateral/insolvency framework) that EBRD uses to argue for specific legal reforms.

entity_name: EBRD news and project announcements for Kosovo banks
source_name: EBRD Transition Report — Kosovo country assessment (annual)
why_relevant: Compact annual chronicle of Kosovo's institutional reform steps, explicitly tracking financial-sector legislation — the 2024-25 assessment records CBK institutional reform and the draft Law on Banks approved in May 2023. Reliable dated timeline of regulatory milestones.

source_name: European Commission — Kosovo Report (annual enlargement package country report, SWD series)
why_relevant: The single most authoritative annual statement of which EU financial-services and AML acquis Kosovo has transposed, what is missing, and what the Commission expects next. Chapter 4 (free movement of capital), Chapter 9 (financial services), Chapter 24 (AML/CFT) and Chapter 32 name specific EU instruments (PSD2/PSR, CRD/CRR, BRRD, AMLD/AMLR, DORA, MiCA) and give forward-looking 'in the coming year' obligations — the earliest reliable deadline signal for Kosovo banking/payments rulemaking.

source_name: Commission Staff Working Document SWD(2024) 243 — assessment of the Reform Agendas (incl. Kosovo)
why_relevant: Contains the Commission's step-by-step assessment of Kosovo's Reform Agenda, which is where individually dated reform steps (including public financial management, digitalisation and business-environment steps that touch payments/e-invoicing/AML) are enumerated.

source_name: European Commission — Enlargement package / EU Enlargement Policy Communication (strategy chapeau)
why_relevant: Sets the region-wide sequencing and any 'gradual integration' offers (e.g. SEPA access, capital-markets and payments integration steps) that determine when Kosovo must have PSD2/AMLR-equivalent rules in force. Cross-country framing often pre-announces conditionality before it appears in national law.

source_name: IMF PIMA / infrastructure governance TA portal — Kosovo documents
why_relevant: Secondary IMF TA channel that publishes Kosovo diagnostic reports outside the main publications feed; useful to catch TA outputs that never appear in the country-report series. Fiscal-governance focus, so relevant mainly as context for state-bank/development-bank plans.

source_name: IMF Financial Sector Stability Review (FSSR) Kosovo and 2026 FSSR Follow-up Technical Assistance Report
why_relevant: The single most detailed external audit of Kosovo's supervisory and macroprudential framework. The 2019 FSSR set the reform agenda; the 2025/2026 follow-up scores implementation and issues a refreshed TA workplan — effectively a forward calendar of regulatory change (SREP, Basel III, resolution, data infrastructure, AML/CFT supervision).

source_name: IMF Article IV Consultation reports and press releases on Republic of Kosovo
why_relevant: Annual diagnostic of the supervisory regime; contains explicit recommendations to CBK on SREP rollout, Basel III elements, crisis management, resolution and financial safety net, frequently with indicative timelines. Often flags draft laws/regulations before CBK publishes them.

source_name: IMF Stand-By Arrangement / Resilience and Sustainability Facility review reports for Kosovo (2023-2025)
why_relevant: Programme documents carry structural benchmarks and RSF reform measures with hard dates — e.g. the fourth-review benchmark requiring a roadmap for adopting the Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process. These convert directly into dated regulatory commitments for CBK and MoF.

source_name: Kosovo trusted-services / electronic-signature legal framework (eIDAS-aligned law, MINT + information-society agency)
why_relevant: Explains Kosovo's law on electronic identification and trusted services (aligned to EU Reg. 910/2014) — qualified e-signature/e-seal equivalence to wet signature, which governs remote onboarding and e-contracting for banks and PSPs. Points to the supervising ministry/agency and to the qualified-provider regime.

source_name: Kallxo.com — legislative-process journalism (draft-law analyses)
why_relevant: Investigative outlet that produces article-by-article analyses of pending Kosovo draft laws, including digital/financial-adjacent bills (e.g. digital signatures and seals — directly relevant to payments authentication). Useful as an early-warning pointer to bills before they surface prominently on institutional sites, and for identifying contested provisions.

entity_name: Kosovo general-news wires covering ATK/MF announcements
source_name: BQK Regional Conference on Crypto-assets and Digital Money (with IMF) — Prishtina
why_relevant: Concrete instance of the weak-signal pattern: a BQK+IMF conference themed 'policy and regulatory frameworks in a changing environment', with IMF's Tobias Adrian and regional governors, held 3-4 June in Prishtina. Signals a crypto-asset/digital-money regulatory workstream ahead of any published rule. Media coverage supplies agenda detail and named participants.

entity_name: Kosovo general-news wires covering ATK/MF announcements
source_name: Albanian-language economic press coverage of IFI reports on Kosovo (Telegrafi, Ekonomia Online, Buletini Ekonomik, Zëri, Kallxo)
why_relevant: Fastest local signal that an IMF/World Bank document has been released, and the only place some IFI findings are summarised in Albanian. Also surfaces documents not indexed on IFI sites (e.g. the IMF Fiscal Transparency Code review published via CBK). Secondary reliability — always trace back to the primary IFI PDF.

source_name: ARKEP — Agjenda Digjitale e Kosovës 2030 (Kosovo Digital Agenda)
why_relevant: Strategy document naming digital-finance and e-payment objectives and the donors backing them (GIZ, World Bank, USAID, SIDA and others are listed as ICT-sector donors). Strategy annexes typically carry an action plan with responsible institutions and deadlines — pre-legislative timetable material touching payments.

source_name: BPB — 'Hyn ne fuqi rregullorja per qasje ne llogari pagese me sherbime bazike' (basic payment account regulation notice)
why_relevant: The single best proof-of-concept for this cell's thesis: a commercial bank page whose headline literally announces that a CBK regulation on access to basic-services payment accounts has entered into force. The bank page names the regulation and the date, which a public rule tracker in Kosovo does not reliably do.

source_name: BPB (Banka per Biznes) — Njoftim mbi IBAN
why_relevant: A dedicated standing customer notice explaining the IBAN conversion mandated by the CBK Regulation on the Standard Bank Account Number System, including the XK05 prefix construction. It is a worked example of a bank restating a regulation in customer-facing language with the operative date.

source_name: BPB — Kushtet dhe afatet e pergjithshme per marredhenien bankare
why_relevant: The bank's general banking-relationship terms, including the clause obliging notification of changes at least 30 days before the effective date (shorter where law or regulator requires). That clause itself is the mechanism this whole cell exploits, and its wording changes when the underlying consumer-protection rule changes.

entity_name: Council of Europe PECK project reports on Kosovo
source_name: Council of Europe PECK project reports on Kosovo (economic crime / AML supervision assessment)
why_relevant: Independent external assessment of how Kosovo authorities including CBK exercise AML/CFT supervision and sanctioning — reveals enforcement practice and weaknesses that CBK's own publications understate, and names the supervisory instruments actually used.

entity_name: Council of Europe PECK project reports on Kosovo
source_name: Council of Europe PECK / PECK II — Kosovo* AML/CFT compliance assessment and follow-up reports (rm.coe.int)
why_relevant: Kosovo is NOT a MONEYVAL member; its FATF-standard evaluation is delivered through the CoE/EU joint 'Project against Economic Crime in Kosovo' (PECK/PECK II) using MONEYVAL methodology. These assessment and follow-up reports produce the recommendations and action-plan dates that become de-facto national AML deadlines. Available in both en and sq.

entity_name: Council of Europe PECK project reports on Kosovo
source_name: Council of Europe ECCD — Kosovo banking-sector AML/CFT capacity workshops (with SHBK)
why_relevant: Donor/standard-setter reporting on joint events with the Kosovo Banking Association, CBK and the Financial Intelligence Unit. These write-ups name the association officials involved (e.g. the SHBK PPP/AML committee chair and CEO) and describe which emerging-technology compliance obligations the industry is being prepared for — a reliable, unblocked mirror of association compliance activity.

source_name: ProCredit Bank Kosovo — General Terms and Conditions PDFs (individuals & businesses)
why_relevant: The versioned T&C PDFs carry an explicit 'in force from' date and a version number (e.g. v1.2). Version-to-version diffs expose exactly which clause changed and when, which is the cleanest indirect read-out of a new CBK rule or payment-services requirement in a market with no consolidated public rule tracker.

source_name: BIS central bankers' speeches referencing Kosovo Banking Association events
why_relevant: CBK governors' speeches delivered at SHBK conferences are archived by BIS in stable, fetchable PDF form. They are the clearest statement of the regulator-to-industry agenda — upcoming rules, transposition timetables and supervisory expectations — and are addressed directly to the association's membership.

source_name: Instituti GAP — analyses of Kosovo's legislative strategy and process
why_relevant: Independent think tank that audits how well the Government's legislative programme is actually executed (slippage rates, bills dropped, consultation quality). Useful as a calibration layer: it tells you how much to discount announced legislative timelines when forecasting when a banking/payments bill will really reach the gazette.

source_name: KoSSev — bilingual (sq/sr) coverage of Kosovo government and Assembly decisions
why_relevant: One of the few outlets covering Kosovo institutional decisions in Serbian alongside Albanian, including government approval of budgets and international financial agreements. Provides sr-language naming of bills and decisions, which helps resolve the same act across the sq/sr official texts.

source_name: Vokshi & Lata Law Firm — Kosovo financial-regulation client alerts (e.g. crypto-asset licensing deadlines)
why_relevant: Local counsel alerts translate BQK/Assembly instruments into concrete compliance deadlines ('what businesses must prepare by December') faster and more explicitly than the regulator does. Useful as a deadline cross-check and as a pointer to instruments you may have missed.

source_name: BIRN Kosovo / KosovaPress (sr edition) — data-protection enforcement reporting
why_relevant: Serbian-language reporting on AIP enforcement (e.g. prohibition on processing biometric data) — the practical route to sr-language coverage of Kosovo regulators, which publish sr versions inconsistently.

source_name: Deutsche Bundesbank — EU-funded ESCB programme for Western Balkans central banks / banking supervisors (Kosovo beneficiary)
why_relevant: Programme announcements and closing events describe exactly which supervisory capabilities BQK was being built up in — banking supervision, financial stability, consumer protection, NPL resolution, payment systems, legislative alignment. That component list is a forward map of Kosovo's supervisory agenda. Bundesbank is the consortium lead and publishes launch/closing press releases with named deliverables.

source_name: ecoi.net — mirrored archive of EU enlargement country reports
why_relevant: Stable third-party archive of Commission country reports with persistent IDs. Useful fallback when enlargement.ec.europa.eu rotates its opaque document-download URLs, which it does between publication cycles.

source_name: European Parliament — reports/resolutions on the Commission Reports on Kosovo (oeil / doceo)
why_relevant: EP resolutions restate and sharpen AML/financial-crime demands on Kosovo and are a pointer into the legislative-observatory trail; useful as a secondary confirmation and for spotting which AML shortcomings are politically salient.

source_name: Fibank Kosova — Kushtet e punes (terms in force from a stated date)
why_relevant: A smaller Kosovo bank (Bulgarian First Investment Bank group) that encodes the effective date directly in the filename ('ne fuqi nga 21 Shkurt 2026'). Smaller banks change terms in lockstep with the sector when a rule bites, so they serve as corroboration that a change is regulation-driven rather than a single bank's commercial decision.

source_name: German Economic Team — Kosovo SEPA accession analysis
why_relevant: Donor-funded advisory that explains the SEPA accession procedure step by step (legislation -> CBK application -> EPC/DG FISMA assessment -> PSP scheme adherence) and dates the regulatory milestones. Useful as a pointer to the specific laws and regulations required.

source_name: GIZ — Improving financial governance in Kosovo (project page)
why_relevant: GIZ project pages state objectives, partners, budget and end dates — a donor timetable that often precedes institutional reform. Scope observed is public financial governance (accountability, transparency, effectiveness) rather than bank supervision, so relevance to A3 is partial but worth a low-frequency watch; GIZ Kosovo's country portfolio page is the pointer to any newer financial-sector project.

source_name: IFC / SECO — Partnership with Central Bank of Kosovo to Advance Digital Financial Services
why_relevant: Donor-project artefact that names the rule under preparation before it exists: IFC with Swiss SECO supporting BQK on a draft law on payment services and open banking, explicitly to create a supportive regulatory environment. This is exactly the pre-legislative signal the cell targets, and IFC/SECO publish project updates and sometimes deliverables.

source_name: ProCredit Holding — Annual Report & Disclosure Report (Pillar 3), Kosovo segment
why_relevant: ProCredit Holding is Frankfurt-listed and BaFin/ECB-supervised, so its annual and Pillar 3 disclosure reports must describe material regulatory developments in each operating country — including Kosovo — in audited, dated English prose. This is the highest-credibility indirect statement of Kosovo regulatory change available anywhere in this cell.

source_name: UNDP Kosovo — Money laundering typologies for Kosovo (Tipologjitë e pastrimit të parave)
why_relevant: Donor-produced typology material developed with/for Kosovo authorities; useful for understanding what predicate-offence patterns the FIU expects banks to detect, and as evidence of the technical-assistance pipeline that usually precedes new FIU guidance.

source_name: World Bank Independent Evaluation Group — Kosovo Country Program Evaluation (FY2012-25)
why_relevant: Independent retrospective on whether World Bank financial-sector interventions in Kosovo achieved their regulatory objectives — reveals which conditionality slipped and which reforms are being re-tabled, a strong predictor of future programme design.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Kosova SHA — Per ne / Legal Notice (corporate transformation disclosure)
why_relevant: Ziraat's own pages disclose that from 19 May 2025 the entity converted from a foreign-bank branch (T.C. Ziraat Bankasi A.S. - Dega ne Kosove) into a Kosovo-registered joint-stock company explicitly to comply with local regulatory standards. That is a licensing/supervision change surfaced by the bank rather than by a public regulator feed — exactly the indirect-mirror pattern, and it dates a branch-to-subsidiary supervisory shift affecting foreign-branch banks generally.
